question.worked_solution:
For a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ where $n$ is the number of trials, and $p$ is the probability of success on each trial,  we have the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x}
$$

Here, we have $X∼B(3,0.4),$ so $X$ has the probability mass function

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{x})(0.4)^{x}(0.6)^{3-x}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0<X\le 2) & =P(X\in \{1,2\}) \\  & =f(1)+f(2) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1})(0.4)^{1}(0.6)^{3-1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2})(0.4)^{2}(0.6)^{3-2} \\  & =3(0.4)^{1}(0.6)^{2}+3(0.4)^{2}(0.6)^{1} \\  & =0.72.\end{aligned}
$$
